new_statements.translation: 4.2 The tones. Two tones, High and Low, can be reconstructed for Proto-Northern-Jos. Low tone is rendered with the grave accent, High tone is left unmarked. In individual daughter languages downstep is also observed, really a mid tone that occurs only after a High tone. It is marked by a vertical stroke before the syllable, e.g. bá'ta (High-Downstep). Proto-Northern-Jos tones are well preserved in the daughter languages. One factor that can disturb tone correspondences in the noun is the tone pattern. All noun prefixes in Proto-Northern-Jos, for example, have Low tone. In some languages, however, the prefix tone is systematically levelled to the stem tone [...]
